pages.text: "I won't brush!" Nils the little bear shook his head by the tub. Blueberry marks dotted his mouth. "Sleepy. I want my bed right now!"
Hoot went the owl. Bedtime. Grandpa Bruno offered a little wooden toothbrush. Nils pretended not to see and hurried up the ladder.
The covers were soft. But something tickled between his teeth. His tongue couldn't push out the daytime blueberries. "Something is stuck here..." His eyes opened wide.
Even closing his eyes didn't bring sleep. He tossed and turned. Grandpa climbed up with a lamp. "Why aren't you sleeping?" "My teeth tickle."
Grandpa brought the lamp close. "Say aaah." Purple dots sat between the teeth. "Those purple dots make your teeth hurt all night."
They went down to the tub. Grandpa wet the brush. "Brush up, brush down. Inside too." "Brush, brush—goodbye, purple!" Nils brushed hard.
Cloudy purple water flowed out. Nils took a sip and spat. Under the lamp, not one purple dot remained. Clean white teeth. "Brush, brush—goodbye, purple!"
The tickly spot was clean. Nils went up to the loft. His tongue felt smooth teeth. "Now I can sleep!" His eyes slowly closed.
Morning: tap, tap, tap from the woodpecker! Nils took his brush first. "One, brush in the morning! Two, brush again when the owl hoots! Three, brush up and down!" Both paws high!

That night, Grandpa gently rubbed his nose to Nils's forehead and tucked him in. Brushing before bed means no tickles and a good sleep. "Brush, brush—goodbye, purple! Sleep tight." Nils closed his eyes.
